source.title: Anomalous transport in the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou model: a review and open problems

accepted.question_text: In the symmetric Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou-β chain, what is the correct universality class governing anomalous heat transport and the associated interface dynamics? More specifically, how should one characterize the large-scale scaling behavior of this model when the observed dynamics disagrees with both Kardar-Parisi-Zhang scaling and the Edwards-Wilkinson analogy predicted by fluctuating hydrodynamics, yet numerical evidence still indicates a transport exponent consistent with kinetic-theory predictions?

evidence.quote: Altogether, a result emerges from these interface-like simulations: the FPUT-β model differs from both the KPZ and EW dynamics, suggesting that it belongs to a different and yet unknown universality class.
Moreover, our equilibrium simulations provide direct evidence that the interface dynamics associated to the FPUT-β model belongs to a further yet unknown universality class.

accepted.question_text: For nonequilibrium heat-transport studies of Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou chains, how do choices in thermostatting protocol—especially the number of thermostatted oscillators and the bath coupling strength—control finite-size corrections and the rate at which the measured flux approaches the asymptotic anomalous-scaling regime, and what simulation procedures remain reliable as the system size changes?

evidence.quote: However, there are no comprehensive studies where the quality of different procedures is discussed especially as a function of the system size.
Hence, the question is the way the asymptotic behavior is progressively reached.

accepted.question_text: When conservative stochastic momentum-exchange noise is added to a nonlinear Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou chain, why can the observed finite-size scaling appear to move toward different effective exponents even though the asymptotic universality class is argued to remain unchanged? Equivalently, what mechanism lets conservative noise alter convergence rates and effective thermal resistance without changing the long-distance hydrodynamic universality class?

evidence.quote: it is unclear the reason why the scaling behavior should be accelerated by the addition of an extra conservative noise, which, a priori, should more reasonably lower the conductivity (increase the thermal resistance).
conservative noise does not change the universality class.

accepted.question_text: For Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou chains close to an integrable limit, such as perturbations of the Toda chain or the harmonic chain, what are the characteristic length scales that determine when transport crosses over from ballistic motion to a kinetic or apparently diffusive finite-size regime and finally to the asymptotic anomalous regime, and how do those scales depend on the strength of the integrability-breaking perturbation?

evidence.quote: A relevant issue regards the typical length scales over which the anomalous transport sets in.

To summarize, upon increasing the lattice size L on should observe three different regimes (see Fig. 12) (i) Ballistic Regime (L < ℓ): Constant heat flux J. (ii) Kinetic/Diffusive Regime (ℓ < L ≤ ℓc): Finite-size effect showing apparent normal diffusion with J ∝ 1/L. (iii) Anomalous Regime (L > ℓc): The asymptotic anomalous component JA ∝ Lδ−1 dominates.

accepted.question_text: What qualitatively new nonequilibrium heat-transport phenomena arise in Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou dynamics when the model is extended to include long-range interactions whose coupling decays as an inverse power of distance, or when disorder and nonlinearity act together in the same system?

evidence.quote: Finally, there is a number of possible new effects that may arise in nonequilibrium FPUT dynamics. We just mention the role of long-range forces, notably coupling which decay as inverse power of the distance [84, 85] and the interplay between disorder and nonlinearity [86, 87].
